timeToCredentials.basis: Our estimate: a Google Cloud project, consent screen and web OAuth client are created in the console with an existing Google account and no review. No source gives a duration.

timeToProduction.basis: Our estimate: a security assessment class is typically four to twelve weeks or more. Google's help page says verification may take several months depending on data sensitivity but gives no number.

humanEffortHours.basis: Our estimate: console setup, scope justification and verification materials, then back-and-forth with reviewers and the assessor. No source gives effort figures.

verdict.summary: Registering the Google OAuth app takes hours, but a server-side agent that reads and sends Gmail for other customers uses restricted scopes. That means Google verification and an annual third-party security assessment, which Google says can take months.
verdict.biggestLaunchRisk: Restricted-scope verification plus the annual third-party security assessment, because the agent stores or transmits Gmail data on your servers. Until it clears, the app is capped at 100 new users and shows an unverified-app screen.

requirements.text: A Google Cloud account and a Google Cloud project.
The app must be registered with Google Auth Platform (OAuth consent screen configured) before an OAuth client can be created.
Agree to the Google API Services User Data Policy during consent screen setup.
Declare the scopes on the consent screen. Scopes must be listed for apps used outside your Workspace organization.
Complete restricted-scope verification, including the additional requirements for restricted scopes in the API Services User Data Policy.
Pass an annual security assessment by a Google-approved third party if restricted data is accessed from or through a third-party server.
Whether a registered legal business entity is required for restricted-scope verification is not stated in the sources.

scopesAndNuances.text: Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes for consumer data must complete verification unless an exception applies. Exceptions include personal use, development/testing, internal use, service-owned data only, and domain-wide installation. A multi-customer SaaS agent likely does not qualify.

Restricted scopes need extra reviews that include a possible security assessment. Apps accessing restricted data from or through a third-party server need an annual assessment by a Google-approved third party.
If the scopes in your code differ from those on the consent screen, users see the unverified-app screen. Keep them identical.
Unverified apps are limited to 100 new users. Google may also reclassify scopes as sensitive or restricted, with a grace period and email notice.

Google Workspace Marketplace review is a separate review for Marketplace listings and typically takes several days. It lists incomplete OAuth verification as a rejection reason. The sources do not say it is needed for Gmail API access.
A developer reported that Shopify app reviewers did not complete a required Gmail OAuth connection and rejected the app. If you also list in a third-party app store, plan a demo mode or demo video.
The sources do not say which individual Gmail scopes are classified as restricted. Check Google's OAuth API verification FAQ scope list for the exact scopes you plan to request.
The provider's published OAuth metadata lists: 3 scope(s) listed; PKCE: plain, S256; no registration endpoint is listed.

blockers.problem: The security assessment applies because the agent stores or transmits restricted Gmail data via servers.
blockers.fix: Plan the assessment early, minimize the data you store and the scopes you request, and document your data handling before engaging a Google-approved assessor.

blockers.problem: The app is unverified, so users see a warning screen and the app is capped at 100 new users.
blockers.fix: Request verification as soon as the consent screen and scopes are final. You can keep building and testing with test users in the meantime.

blockers.problem: Requested scopes in code do not match the consent screen scopes.
blockers.fix: Align the scopes in your code with those selected on the consent screen.

blockers.problem: It is unclear whether Google requires a legal business entity for restricted-scope verification.
blockers.fix: Ask Google through the verification process, or check the policy pages, before committing to a launch date.
